mcqs.question: A CPU is at 60% utilization but has a deep, growing work queue. Which framework surfaces this as a problem, and why?
options: Neither framework can detect this since 60% utilization looks healthy either way
RED, because Rate would show the CPU is a bottleneck
USE, because its Saturation signal specifically captures queued/waiting work, which utilization alone doesn't show
USE, because Errors would already be firing in this scenario
mcqs.explanation: USE's Saturation dimension exists precisely to catch this case -- utilization alone can look fine while queued work reveals a real bottleneck. RED is built for request-driven services, not resource-level queueing, and Errors wouldn't necessarily be firing yet.

mcqs.question: A team's service dashboard has grown to 40 panels over time. What's the actual problem, and the fix?
options: The dashboard should be split into 40 separate dashboards, one per panel
The problem is that 40 panels is too many to fit on one screen resolution
The fix is to delete most of the historical data being displayed
There's no clear top-level 'is it broken' signal buried among the panels; the fix is a hierarchy with one RED-based health signal up top and the rest one click deeper
mcqs.explanation: The core issue is missing hierarchy/prioritization, not screen size or data retention -- a clear top-level signal with detail panels one click away fixes the actual on-call usability problem without losing any data or fragmenting the dashboard uselessly.
